mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.25%, it reduces real interest rates, thereby increasing the present value of expected corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day prior window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor-market strengthening events, the SPX 20-day forward return is negative or flat (quantile regression slope < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) of at least 3% for three consecutive months predicts a temporary boost in investor sentiment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥3% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During the 5-day window following the trigger, SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior 5-day window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeding 102.0 while inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 4.0 indicates a supply-side expansion that outpaces price pressures, producing a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In 50% of similar supply-side expansion events, the SPX 20-day forward return is negative or flat (quantile regression 50th percentile ≤ 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for two consecutive months typically coincides with a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and dampens equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.3 percentage points in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior 60-day window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) miss by more than 50,000 jobs in a month while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 4%, it signals a weak labor market and triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In 70% of similar labor-market miss events, the SPX 20-day forward return is non-negative (quantile regression 30th percentile ≥ 0).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in retail sales (HOUST) of 2% or more for four consecutive months suggests a cooling demand environment, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥2% month-over-month for four consecutive months
failure_condition: During the 5-day window following the trigger, SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 5-day window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls by more than 5% in a month while the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains flat, it indicates a supply shock that raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, producing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >5% AND CPIAUCSL shows no month-over-month change
failure_condition: In 80% of analogous supply-shock events, the SPX 20-day forward return is non-negative (quantile regression 20th percentile ≥ 0).
